## Goal

Document exactly what the headless arena now models (full campaign progression via the shared sequencer, hold-full upgrade choices) and what remains simplified (VFX, formations, mini-boss/boss, rendering), so consumers never over-read the balance report (parent AC6/AC9). Update `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`, README, and the relevant code comments, and keep the docs guards green.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** `docs/BALANCING.md` documents the fidelity boundary exactly: what campaign behaviour is now modelled (waves/levels via the shared sequencer incl. fixed/curve/dynamic; upgrade choices via the shared choice flow) and what remains simplified (boss/mini-boss, VFX, formations, rendering), so consumers do not over-read the report; `waveReached`/`levelReached`/`upgradesSelected` are now populated from campaign runs.
- **AC2:** `docs/EVALUATION.md` (or the balancing doc if it owns batch semantics) documents `--batch` = full campaign by default and `--skirmish` opt-out, plus the bounded tick budget and how to read the per-wave/per-level distributions.
- **AC3:** README and key code comments (arena/engine/report) reflect the new default without stale skirmish-only claims.
- **AC4:** All related documentation is updated (code comments, `docs/BALANCING.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`, README), with no stale skirmish-only claims remaining.
- **AC5:** The docs guards (`balancingDocs.test.ts`, `evaluationDocs.test.ts`) pass; no unrelated doc changes were made.

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — fidelity boundary + batch/campaign semantics
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` — batch default, --skirmish, bounded budget, distribution reading
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts`, `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` — code comments reflecting the boundary
- `src/ai/eval/balancingDocs.test.ts`, `src/ai/eval/evaluationDocs.test.ts` — docs guards keep green

# Test: wrapAware config plumbing

Test-first verification slice for the `wrapAware` parameter (parent AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8, AC1 + AC5). Pins the data-driven boolean's default, seed exclusions, CSV wiring and editor exposure **before** the implementation item lands, so the pipeline change is driven by failing tests.

## Goal

Pin the full config pipeline for `wrapAware`: default `true`, `march`/`centipede` seeded `false`, CSV persist + round-trip, editor-panel visibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A test asserts a generic archetype resolves `wrapAware === true` when the field is absent from its seed config.
- Tests assert the `march` and `centipede` seed configs carry `wrapAware === false` (the explicit exclusion list).
- A CSV round-trip test asserts a `wrapAware` column persists and reloads through the config CSV path; a missing/empty value falls back to `true`.
- A test asserts the field is enumerable through the existing `EnemyConfig` editor/config plumbing without extra per-field admin.
- All tests pass deterministically (no wall clock, no RNG).

## Key Files

- `src/core/configTypes.ts`
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts`
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`
- `src/core/enemyConfig.ts`
- `src/utils/csvEdit.ts`

# Same resolver in the game, the level gym and the enemy editor

**Parent:** AH-0MVJ8W4GE007OMNT (AC4).
**Depends on:** Entity force-field layer (AH-0MVM8GUZG008AWSU), Shared force-field bubble feedback (AH-0MVM8GW7W004SI0E).

## Goal

As a developer, I want the force-field resolution to run once in shared code
and be consumed by `PlayScene` and the gyms, so enabled behaviour is identical
everywhere and only a documented disabled/override case diverges.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC4 — Gym parity and tunability.** The same resolver drives the game and the level gym, with a parity test and gym-editor controls.
- `PlayScene._spawnEnemy` resolves `enemyForceFieldHits(waveManager.level, cfg)`
  at spawn and passes the result into `createEnemyFromConfig` — the run level
  comes from `WaveManager`, never a hard-coded value.
- `GymLevel` (which launches real campaign waves) uses the **same** resolver
  with its launched level, through the same factory path.
- `GymFodderEnemies` gains force-field controls in `ENEMY_SLIDER_RANGES` so a
  formation-gym spawn (no campaign context) can force a field on with a chosen
  hit count. The divergence — the gym slider sets hits **directly** instead of
  evaluating the level curve — is documented in the code next to the control
  and in the gym panel copy, and must never leak into the shipped campaign CSV.
- A parity test in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` asserts the
  same (level, config) pair yields the same field hits in the game path and the
  gym path; the ram-absorb behaviour is asserted identical in both (it lives in
  the shared core).
- The duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity
  docs assertion stay green.
- Resolved field strength is deterministic for a fixed/curve campaign: same
  level + seed ⇒ identical shields.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (+ `PlayScene.test.ts`).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymLevel.ts` (+ `.test.ts`); `GymBotTuning`/`GymCurveSequencer`
  if they spawn campaign waves.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFodderEnemies.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — editor controls.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — parity block.
data.title: Game and gym spawn parity

# Documentation, tuning table and balance evidence

**Parent:** AH-0MVJ8W4GE007OMNT (AC5).
**Depends on:** Game and gym spawn parity (AH-0MVM8GXEF009883O).

## Goal

As a balance engineer and a future maintainer, I want the new enemy barrier
documented with a tuning table and backed by bot-batch evidence, so the
behaviour is discoverable and the campaign stays playable.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC5 — Verification and documentation.** Unit tests cover the resolver curve, codec, entity and scene integration, and the GDD/enemy docs are updated.
- GDD `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.6 no longer claims "no shield layer"
  and describes the enemy force field (barrier first, hull second, ram absorb);
  §4.1 carries the tuning values and the formula.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` gains a section with the behaviour,
  the per-archetype tuning table (start level, start hits, max hits, cap 5),
  the ram rule (Q6 = B, one hit per contact with the re-arm) and the feedback
  surface; the gym-editor divergence is recorded.
- The CSV header comments in `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` document the three
  columns and their neutral defaults.
- A bot-batch evidence run at **L1/L5/L10** records `survivalSeconds`,
  `levelReached`, `avoidableHits` and `enemiesKilledByArchetype`, recorded as a
  comment on this item with the command used and before/after values; L1 is
  demonstrated unchanged. Evidence is **advisory** (no numeric pass/fail gate)
  except that L1 must be identical to the pre-change baseline.
- The docs assertions (`balancingDocs`, `evaluationDocs`, roster docs) stay
  green and the **full project test suite passes** with the changes.

## Key Files

- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` — header comments.
- `src/ai/eval/`, `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — L1/L5/L10 evidence mode.
data.title: Docs, tuning table, bot-batch evidence

data.comment:
Design decision (recorded before coding): the headless arena (src/ai/eval/arena.ts) currently models hostiles hull-only (hostile.health -= 1 per player bullet; Key Files lists src/ai/eval/ for the L1/L5/L10 evidence mode). Without a barrier layer the before/after evidence at L5/L10 would be trivially identical, and the AC requires meaningful before/after values with only L1 identical to the pre-change baseline.

Plan for the evidence mode:
1. Give the arena Hostile a resolved forceFieldHits from the SAME shared enemyForceFieldHits(level, cfg) curve the game uses — deterministic, pure, Phaser-free (fits the pure-eval-core guard).
2. Spend field hits before hull in the bullet-vs-hostile collision (mirrors BaseEnemy.takeDamage: barrier first, hull second).
3. Add forceFields:boolean to ArenaConfig/BatchConfig/CliOptions/evaluate.mjs with --force-fields on|off; off resolves all barriers at level 1 (= 0 hits for every shipped archetype since min startLevel is 2 or 0) so a PRE-CHANGE baseline is captured with identical harness code and seeds (exactly the --scale-levels off precedent). L1 is byte-identical on/off by construction.
4. Docs: GDD 2.6 (remove 'no shield layer'), GDD 4.1 tuning values + formula, enemy-guide section + per-archetype tuning table + ram rule Q6=B (one field hit per contact, 500ms re-arm, ENEMY_FIELD_RAM_REARM_MS) + feedback surface + gym-editor divergence (GymFodderEnemies gymDirectForceFieldHits sets hits directly, never evaluates the curve).
5. Docs guard test (balancingDocs/evaluationDocs/roster docs stay green; add enemy-force-field docs assertions).
6. Evidence comment with command used + before/after values.
